title: South Korean online commerce expands through mobile services while clothing contracts and mobile share edges down
source_unit: South Korea Ministry of Data and Statistics Online Shopping Trends, July 2026

denominator.unit: aggregate South Korean online-shopping transaction value; not household respondents

mobile_share_of_online_shopping.unit: percent of online-shopping transaction value; 78.6% a year earlier

observations.method: South Korean official online-shopping trends release, using transaction-value estimates by product group and operating form; mobile share is reported within total online-shopping transaction value.
observations.uncertainty: These are aggregate transaction values, not unique consumers, household welfare, or real-volume measures. Nominal growth can reflect prices, product mix, and platform coverage; a mobile-share decline does not establish less mobile use by individual consumers.
observations.subgroup: South Korean online-shopping market and mobile channel; no consumer-income, age, household, or regional subgroup in the headline release.
observations.counterinterpretation: Online growth can coexist with affordability pressure if essential services, delivery, or price inflation lead the increase; platform transaction value does not show merchant margins, consumer debt, or satisfaction.

observations.period: July 2026; online product and service categories

denominator.unit: aggregate South Korean online-shopping category transaction values; nominal year-over-year changes

observations.method: Official category-level online-shopping transaction-value comparisons from the July 2026 release.
observations.uncertainty: Category movement is nominal and platform-based; it does not distinguish price, order count, basket size, or whether online categories replace offline purchases. Month-over-month travel and food-service changes may be seasonal.
observations.subgroup: South Korean online product and service categories.
observations.counterinterpretation: Food delivery/grocery and auto-goods growth may reflect convenience, price, or repair/replacement cycles rather than stronger household discretionary room; clothing decline can reflect seasonality or promotions.

related_sources.claim: Official South Korean statistical release reports July 2026 total, mobile, category, and operating-form online-shopping transaction values.
KOSIS is the official Korean statistical portal linked by the release for statistical tables and supporting datasets.

boundary: This record adds a South Korean mobile-commerce and service-category layer to Hong Kong category polarization and Japan household/channel contraction. It does not measure unique consumers, cultural attendance, household welfare, causal platform substitution, or merchant value capture.
